To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sensitivity of NGF- responsive dorsal root ganglion neurons to semaphorins is maintained in both neonatal and adult mice.
semaphorin A, D, or E can inhibit axonal growth of NGF-responsive neurons from both neonatal and adult DRGs.
semaphorin receptors, neuropilins and PlexinA1, are present in the DRGs in both the adult and neonatal mice and that semaphorins inhibit axonal growth in vitro from neonatal and adult DRG neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the neurotrophin nerve growth factor (NGF) in the development of sympathetic neurons.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying the growth, guidance and targeting of developing axons and the role of these processes in establishing the nervous system of the vertebrate embryo.
the development and function of sensory neurons in the dorsal root ganglia (DRG), and in particular with the role of neurotrophins in the survival of DRG neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sensitivity of NGF-responsive DRG neurons to semaphorins is maintained throughout development.
semaphorins are not involved in the regulation of the growth of DRG axons in the PNS.
semaphorins are not involved in the development of the peripheral nervous system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
semaphorins D and E are not involved in the development of the sensory nervous system, but they may be involved in the maintenance of adult sensory pathways.
semaphorins are not only expressed in the nervous system but also are able to regulate the growth of sensory axons.
semaphorin responsiveness of DRG neurons is not altered in the transition from neonatal to adult life.
The main takeaway from our work is that

semaphorin-mediated axon guidance in vivo and in vitro is not restricted to the developing nervous system, but may also play a role in the maintenance and regeneration of peripheral nerves in adult animals.
semaphorin-mediated repulsive cues can be effective in inhibiting growth of axons of DRG neurons even in adult animals.
the ability of semaD to act as a repulsive cue for DRG growth is maintained in the adult.
